terms.gloss: a channel, a conduit, a pipe; a canal
terms.comment: Any pipe or channel, open or closed, especially for water; rarely feminine in Cato and Varro (Lewis & Short). The modern languages use it for a television channel, which here is statiō (see channel).

terms.gloss: a brook; a channel for irrigation
terms.comment: A small stream, natural or led off by hand to water the fields.

terms.gloss: a ditch, a dug channel, a canal
terms.comment: Anything dug, from a ditch to a canal (see trench).

phrases.latin: Claudite jam rīvōs, puerī; sat prāta bibērunt.
phrases.english: Close the channels now, boys: the meadows have drunk enough.

sources: Lewis & Short: canalis · Lewis & Short: rivus · Lewis & Short: fossa
